results.title: Ghana’s UN Mission visits family of Ghanaian killed in second Bronx tragedy, pledges support
results.content: Ghana's Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York has visited the family of 24-year-old Ghanaian caregiver Joseph Owusu, who was reportedly killed in the Bronx. Joseph Owusu's death comes days after the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Ghanaian Javits Frimpong in the Bronx on October 29, 2026. The two deaths have raised concern among Ghanaians in New York and relatives in Ghana, with calls for investigations and accountability. The visit, led by Deputy Permanent Representative Ben Dotsel Malor and Consul-General Anthony El-Adas, was undertaken on behalf of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, who joined by phone to express his condolences.

results.title: Beyond the bungalow gates: Why comprehensive sex education and sex negotiation skills are our children’s real protective armor
results.content: The horrifying revelations emerging from Obuasi Senior High Technical School, where up to 19 female students have reportedly come forward detailing alleged sexual exploitation and abuse by members of the school's leadership. Such a report should send chills down the spine of every parent, educator, and policymaker in Ghana. For far too long, our cultural reflex has been one of uncomfortable silence. We treat conversations about adolescent sexuality as a taboo subject. We whisper about puberty behind closed doors while continuing to believe that our teenagers live in a vacuum of innocence. The tragedy at Obuasi SHTS demonstrates that our silence is not protecting our children; it is leaving them defenseless in the face of predatory power dynamics.

results.title: Bagbin is pursuing parliamentary bullying – says Afenyo-Markin
results.content: Minority Leader Osahen Alexander Afenyo-Markin has accused Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin of presiding over what he describes as parliamentary bullying, following the removal of Damongo MP and Ranking Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abu Jinapor, from the parliamentary chamber on Tuesday. results.title: Traditional media advertising model is failing – MFWA’s Kwaku Krobea
results.content: The traditional media advertising model is failing as advertisers increasingly turn to digital platforms that offer more precise audience targeting and greater flexibility, the Media Foundation for West Africa's (MFWA) Programmes Manager, Kwaku Krobea, has said. He said platforms such as YouTube and Facebook allow advertisers to monitor audience figures in real time and target specific groups based on demographics, interests, purchasing preferences and other audience characteristics. Speaking on Joy Prime's Money Making Monday, Mr Krobea said these capabilities were putting traditional media organisations at a disadvantage in the competition for advertising revenue. “Frankly, sorry, frankly, that business model is failing. And there are no two ways about that,” he said.

results.title: JoyNews Impact Maker Awardee HOL screens 400 women for breast and cervical cancer in Zebilla
results.content: JoyNews Impact Maker Awardee Haven of Love Children’s Foundation (HOL) has screened 400 women for breast and cervical cancer during a two-day free health outreach in Zebilla in the Upper East Region. The exercise, held on October 28 and 29, 2026, at the Church of Pentecost Auditorium, was organised in collaboration with the Bawku West District Health Directorate’s Zebilla Town Clinic as part of activities marking Breast and Cervical Cancer Awareness Month. All 400 participants received both breast and cervical cancer screening, alongside health education and referral support.
